subject: Animation
title: Yuri Norstein: Russia's Animation Treasure
description: A micro-lesson that makes Yuri Norstein: Russia's Animation Treasure usable.

hook.text: Yuri Norstein's 1975 short Hedgehog in the Fog was voted the greatest animated film of all time by peers.

buildup.text: Norstein uses layered glass and cutout animation, creating a unique visual depth that no one has replicated.

discovery.text: Japanese animation master Miyazaki has publicly called Norstein the greatest animator alive.

twist.text: Norstein has been working on his feature film The Overcoat since 1981. It is still unfinished after 40 years.

climax.text: Norstein's perfectionism and limited output have only increased his legendary status among animators.

punchline.text: The greatest animator alive has one unfinished masterpiece.

quiz.question: What makes Yuri Norstein legendary among animators?
options: He created the first CGI animated short
His Hedgehog in the Fog was voted the greatest animated film by peers, and Miyazaki calls him the greatest
He directed the highest-grossing animated film in Russia

details.summary: Yuri Norstein created Hedgehog in the Fog and Tale of Tales, consistently ranked among the greatest animated films ever made. His meticulous layered-glass technique produces dreamlike imagery of extraordinary beauty and emotional depth.
details.whyItMatters: Norstein represents the pinnacle of animation as personal art. His films achieve emotional and visual depth that industrial animation rarely approaches, demonstrating that the greatest animation emerges from individual artistic vision.
takeaways: Norstein's films are consistently ranked among the greatest animations ever made
His layered-glass technique creates uniquely dreamlike visual atmospheres
He has spent decades on his unfinished masterpiece The Overcoat

faq.question: Why is Hedgehog in the Fog so highly regarded?
faq.answer: In just ten minutes, Norstein creates an atmosphere of wonder, fear, and beauty through a hedgehog's walk through fog. The layered glass creates actual depth and light diffusion. It was voted the greatest animated film of all time by 140 animators and film critics.

faq.question: Why has Norstein's The Overcoat taken so long?
faq.answer: Norstein has been working on his adaptation of Gogol's The Overcoat since 1981. His refusal to compromise his painstaking technique means each second takes enormous effort. The unfinished film has become legendary, representing both artistic perfectionism and its costs.
